About Dominique Duncan-Nelson



Her services include buying, selling, leasing, property management (short-, mid-, and long-term, including Airbnb), and interior design.She is based in Chatsworth, serving Porter Ranch, Granada Hills, Northridge, Sylmar, San Fernando, Mission Hills, Encino, Sherman Oaks, Studio City, Tarzana, Woodland Hills, and Burbank.Dominique brings a background that most agents simply don't have. She holds a Bachelor of Science in Business and a degree in Marketing — a foundation she built on early and has carried into every chapter of her career since.
From there, she went on to hold management and human resources leadership roles at one of the world's most recognizable brands — a Fortune Global 500 company — where she developed the organizational skills, negotiation strength, and professionalism that define her work with clients today.
She then took those skills and built and operated a successful property management company that earned over 900 five-star reviews, giving her clients a distinct advantage when buying, selling, or transitioning into investment properties. Her path into real estate sales was a natural evolution — she entered the industry as an investor and property operator, not a salesperson.


Dominique is also a homeowner herself, and a wife and mother of two. Her personal experience navigating homeownership, building businesses, and planning for her family's future gives her a genuine perspective on what her clients are working toward — not just the transaction, but the life on the other side of it.

For Buyers:Dominique specializes in first-time home buyers throughout the San Fernando Valley. She is patient, education-focused, and committed to helping clients understand both their short-term needs and long-term financial goals. She integrates budgeting, equity planning, and future rental considerations into every buyer consultation.
For Sellers:She offers professional staging coordination, high-quality marketing, virtual tours, AI pricing tools, and strategic open houses designed to attract serious buyers. Her structured approach emphasizes organization, negotiation strength, and clear communication.

Clients consistently describe her as responsive, honest, organized, and strategic.If you are looking for a San Fernando Valley real estate agent serving Los Angeles County — including Chatsworth, Porter Ranch, West Hills, Canoga Park, Woodland Hills, Northridge, Granada Hills, and surrounding communities — who understands property from both the transaction and ownership side, Dominique is ready to guide you.

bank-statement-loans.html.main_text: Bank Statement Mortgages for Self Employed BuyersSome lenders offer bank statement programs for self employed borrowers. They evaluate documented cash flow under their own rules. Deposits are not automatically treated as qualifying income.Start with how income is documentedExplain your business structure and income pattern to the lender. Ask which statements are required, how business expenses are treated, and how transfers or unusual deposits are reviewed.Compare the costs and termsA bank statement option can differ from conventional financing in its rate, down payment, reserves, and fees. Ask the lender to compare it with any standard loan you may qualify for.ConsiderationTraditional documentationBank statement programIncome evidenceTax and employment documentationAccount history and business informationIncome calculationProgram underwriting rulesLender’s deposit and expense analysisTermsDepend on the loan programVary substantially by lenderCalifornia and San Fernando Valley contextFor a San Fernando Valley purchase, the lender determines eligibility and loan terms, while the property can add costs such as taxes, HOA dues, insurance, repairs, and appraisal related issues. Compare written lender disclosures with the full cost of the specific home.Understanding Written Loan TermsCompare financing using the written terms for your application and property. The loan amount, repayment period, rate structure, mortgage insurance, lender charges, and cash required at closing work together. A change in one part of the offer can affect the others, so a quoted monthly principal and interest payment is only part of the comparison.Ask which conditions remain before approval and what changes require a new review. New debt, a change in employment or documented income, or a property issue can affect financing before closing. Use the lender’s current disclosures and explanations rather than relying on a general program description as a promise of eligibility or final terms.Looking Beyond an Approval AmountA lender evaluates whether a mortgage meets its underwriting requirements, while your household budget also includes expenses that may not appear in that calculation. Consider utilities, transportation, healthcare, childcare, maintenance, and the savings you want to preserve. A payment can meet a lending rule and still feel uncomfortable in daily life.Use current information for the particular property, including taxes, insurance, association dues, and any known repairs. Leave room for changes rather than assuming that every expense will stay fixed. Comparing the full monthly picture and the cash remaining after a move makes it easier to recognize the difference between a qualified purchase and a sustainable one.SourcesConsumer Financial Protection Bureau, Buying a HomeConsumer Financial Protection Bureau, Loan EstimatesYour Financing OptionsReview the financing resources and connect with a lender when you are ready.Connect With a Lender

blog/can-the-dodgers-do-a-threepeat-2026.main_text: Can the Dodgers Do a Threepeat?September 28, 2026Why this run is historically differentThe Dodgers are not simply trying to win another World Series. They are trying to become the first Major League team since the 1998 through 2000 Yankees to win three championships in a row. Los Angeles entered October as the back to back defending champion, and no National League team has completed a World Series threepeat.That puts this roster in a rare position. The Dodgers have championship experience, a roster built to win now, and the pressure of knowing every opponent would love to be the team that ends the run.The lineup is still loadedThe Dodgers postseason lineup starts with Mookie Betts, Shohei Ohtani, Will Smith and Freddie Freeman, with Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker, Andy Pages, Max Muncy and Tommy Edman adding depth behind them.October games are not always won with three home runs. Sometimes the difference is one walk, one double, one sacrifice fly or one mistake by the other team. The Dodgers have enough experienced hitters that they do not have to rely on only one person.The rotation gives them a real chanceThe Dodgers carried Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow as their four primary starters for the Division Series. Shohei Ohtani also gives Los Angeles another elite pitching option as a two way player.That kind of depth can change a short postseason series because an opponent may go several days without seeing a comfortable pitching matchup.The bullpen still has to finish the jobThe Dodgers Division Series bullpen includes Edwin Díaz, Tanner Scott, Roki Sasaki, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Edgardo Henriquez, Kris Bubic and Brock Stewart.One walk or one misplaced pitch can change an entire playoff game. A third straight championship will require clean late innings when the margin is smallest.Atlanta is already making them workThe first two games of the Division Series showed why a threepeat is so difficult. Los Angeles won Game 1 against Atlanta, 5 to 3, then the Braves answered in Game 2, 3 to 2. The series moved to Atlanta tied.Six months of regular season work can come down to a handful of pitches, one defensive mistake or one cold night at the plate.What would a third straight title mean?A third championship in a row would move this Dodgers era from a great run into a piece of baseball history. It would also make Los Angeles the first National League club to win three straight World Series titles.The Dodgers have the lineup, the pitching and the championship experience. What they still need is another full October where the biggest players stay healthy, the bullpen survives close games and the offense delivers when one run matters more than ten.So, can they actually do it?Yes, they can. But being talented enough to win and actually winning three championships in a row are two very different things.That is why this postseason is worth watching. A threepeat is not expected. It would be historic, and the Dodgers still have to earn every step of it.ReferencesMLB, Dodgers 2026 Postseason FAQMLB, Dodgers 2026 NL Division Series RosterMLB, Dodgers 2026 Postseason Rotation OutlookMLB, Dodgers Starting Lineups and NLDS ResultsExplore MoreBlogBuyingSelling

blog/coffee-or-tea.html.main_text: Coffee or Tea?September 29, 2026Most people already have a preferenceCoffee or tea sounds like a simple question, but the answer usually comes down to routine, flavor, caffeine, and the kind of morning you like to have.Coffee tends to feel stronger and more direct. Tea can feel lighter and slower. Both can be part of the same morning ritual, just in very different ways.Coffee usually brings more caffeineIf the goal is a stronger caffeine boost, coffee usually wins. The Food and Drug Administration lists regular brewed coffee at roughly 113 to 247 milligrams of caffeine in a 12 ounce serving, while black tea is typically around 71 milligrams and green tea around 37 milligrams.The exact amount depends on the drink, serving size, brewing method, and brand, so the cup in front of you can be very different from an average number.Tea gives you more ways to change the experienceTea can be black, green, white, herbal, spiced, floral, iced, hot, sweetened, or completely plain. Some teas contain caffeine and some herbal teas do not, which makes tea easier to adjust depending on the time of day.It can also be as simple as dropping a tea bag into hot water and letting it steep while you get ready for the day.Coffee has its own ritualFor coffee drinkers, the smell can be part of the appeal before the first sip. Grinding beans, starting a coffee maker, using a French press, or stopping at the same cafe can become part of the morning itself.Coffee can also change dramatically depending on how it is prepared. A plain brewed cup, espresso, latte, cold brew, and cappuccino can all feel like completely different drinks.What about health and caffeine?For most adults, the Food and Drug Administration says 400 milligrams of caffeine per day is an amount not generally associated with negative effects. Individual sensitivity varies, and caffeine can affect sleep, anxiety, heart rate, and digestion differently from person to person.That means the better choice may have less to do with coffee versus tea and more to do with how much caffeine you are actually drinking and how your body responds to it.Coffee or tea at home can also be about convenienceA basic cup of either drink can be inexpensive at home. The cost changes when specialty equipment, premium beans, loose leaf tea, syrups, milk, cafe visits, or multiple drinks per day become part of the routine.If convenience matters most, both can be very easy. A coffee maker can be ready in minutes, and a tea bag only needs hot water and a little time to steep.So, coffee or tea?Choose coffee if you like a bolder flavor, a stronger caffeine lift, and the ritual that comes with brewing it. Choose tea if you want more variety, a gentler caffeine option, or something that can easily shift from morning to evening.Or keep both in the kitchen. Some mornings call for coffee, some afternoons call for tea, and there is no rule saying you have to pick only one.ReferencesU.S. Food and Drug Administration, How Much Caffeine Is Too Much?Explore MoreBlogSearch HomesContact

blog/football-season-is-back-does-your-t.main_text: Football Season Is Back, Does Your Team Play at SoFi This Year?September 27, 2026Does your team play at SoFi this year?SoFi Stadium is home to both the Rams and Chargers, which means Southern California gets a long list of visiting NFL teams every season. If you follow a team outside Los Angeles, this is the part of the schedule worth checking.Below are the remaining regular season games at SoFi as of October 5, 2026, with the quarterbacks, standout offensive and defensive names, and the reason each matchup is interesting.Denver Broncos at Los Angeles Chargers, October 11Denver is led by quarterback Bo Nix, with Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle among the names to know on offense. Cornerback Pat Surtain II remains one of the biggest names on the Broncos defense. The Chargers counter with Justin Herbert, Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston on offense, with Derwin James Jr. leading the secondary.This is an AFC West division game, so it carries extra weight before you even get to the individual matchups.Buffalo Bills at Los Angeles Rams, October 12Buffalo brings Josh Allen to SoFi for Monday Night Football. James Cook is a major part of the backfield, while DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Dalton Kincaid give Allen multiple targets. Greg Rousseau and Bradley Chubb are two of the defensive names to know.The Rams are led by Matthew Stafford, with Puka Nacua and Kyren Williams among their offensive playmakers. This is one of the biggest star power games on the SoFi calendar, and the Monday night stage makes it even bigger.Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams, October 18Arizona has Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, with Trey McBride, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson among the passing game names to know. Budda Baker remains the centerpiece of the Cardinals secondary.This is an NFC West division game. That makes it important beyond one Sunday because the result directly affects the division race.Los Angeles Chargers at Los Angeles Rams, November 1This is the unusual one. The Rams are the designated home team, but the Chargers are not really traveling. Both teams use SoFi Stadium as their home field.Matthew Stafford and Justin Herbert give the game two established quarterbacks, while Puka Nacua, Kyren Williams, Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston give both offenses recognizable playmakers. It is only the second regular season meeting between the two teams at SoFi.Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers, November 8Houston is led by C.J. Stroud, who entered October with 1,141 passing yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions through four games. Will Anderson Jr. had four sacks through his first three games and remains one of the Texans biggest defensive threats.For the Chargers, this creates a quarterback matchup between Stroud and Herbert, with two teams that have young, high profile talent on both sides of the ball.New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers, November 22The Jets offense is led by Geno Smith, with Garrett Wilson, Breece Hall and rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq among the names to know. On defense, Minkah Fitzpatrick gives New York an established playmaker in the secondary.For Jets fans living in Southern California, this is the local chance to see New York without planning a cross country trip.Green Bay Packers at Los Angeles Rams, November 25Green Bay comes to SoFi on Thanksgiving Eve with Jordan Love at quarterback. The Packers are one of the NFL's most recognizable franchises and bring a national fan base wherever they play.The Wednesday night date and holiday timing make this one of the most unusual games on the Rams schedule.New England Patriots at Los Angeles Chargers, November 29New England comes to SoFi for Sunday Night Football. Drake Maye leads the Patriots offense, with Hunter Henry among the veteran targets. Christian Barmore and Kevin Byard III are established names on the defensive side.The primetime slot and New England's national following make this one of the Chargers more noticeable home dates.Kansas City Chiefs at Los Angeles Rams, December 3Patrick Mahomes comes to SoFi for Thursday Night Football. Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy are among the offensive names to know, while Chris Jones and Nick Bolton remain major pieces of the Chiefs defense.Mahomes in Los Angeles automatically makes this one of the marquee games on the Rams schedule.San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Chargers, December 17San Francisco brings Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle to SoFi. Nick Bosa and Fred Warner remain two of the biggest defensive names on the roster.The 49ers have a huge California following, so this Thursday night game should bring plenty of red into the stadium.Dallas Cowboys at Los Angeles Rams, December 20Dallas is led by Dak Prescott, with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens giving the Cowboys a high profile receiving group. On defense, Quinnen Williams and Rashan Gary are two of the major names in the front.The Cowboys have one of the largest national fan bases in football, so a late December visit to SoFi should feel like a major event even before the playoff picture is considered.Kansas City Chiefs at Los Angeles Chargers, Week 17Kansas City returns to SoFi later in the season, this time to play the Chargers. The exact date and kickoff time are still to be announced.This is an AFC West division game, and Mahomes versus Herbert gives it an obvious quarterback storyline. Depending on the standings by late December, it could also have major division or playoff implications.Seattle Seahawks at Los Angeles Rams, Week 18Seattle closes the Rams regular season home schedule at SoFi. Sam Darnold leads the Seahawks offense, while Jaxon Smith Njigba entered October with 405 receiving yards and six touchdowns through three games. Devon Witherspoon is one of Seattle's standout defensive backs.Because this is an NFC West game in Week 18, it has the potential to matter a lot. The exact date and kickoff time are still to be announced.Which game would you choose?Bills fans get Josh Allen on Monday night. Packers fans get Thanksgiving Eve. Chiefs fans have two different chances to see Kansas City in Los Angeles. Cowboys and 49ers fans get late season trips to SoFi.If your team is on the schedule, you do not have to plan a flight across the country to see them. They are coming to Los Angeles.ReferencesLos Angeles Rams, 2026 ScheduleLos Angeles Chargers, 2026 ScheduleBuffalo Bills, 2026 RosterArizona Cardinals, 2026 Team StatisticsDenver Broncos, 2026 RosterHouston Texans, C.J. blog/halloween-san-fernando-valley-2026..main_text: Halloween Activities in and Around the San Fernando ValleySeptember 24, 2026Updated October 14, 2026Halloween around the San Fernando Valley can mean a glowing pumpkin trail, a movie under the stars, or an evening at a community event. The most enjoyable choice depends on the kind of experience your group wants, from a relaxed seasonal outing to a deliberately frightening attraction.October also gives you more than one opportunity to celebrate. A planned evening earlier in the month can leave Halloween night free for your own neighborhood, without trying to combine a major attraction, dinner, and trick or treating into one rushed trip.Pumpkin displays beyond the neighborhood porchNight of the Jack at King Gillette Ranch in Calabasas offers a walking experience built around illuminated pumpkin displays. Its ranch setting makes it a different outing from visiting a decorated residential street, with the landscape and changing light becoming part of the evening.Think about the walk as well as the photographs. Comfortable shoes, your group’s preferred pace, and the time of entry all influence the experience. Before booking, use the organizer’s schedule to confirm the operating date, arrival arrangements, accessibility information, and any rules about what visitors may bring.Calabasas is a nearby destination for a Valley outing, so allow for the journey as part of the plan. A ticketed visit works best when there is enough time to arrive without turning the first part of the evening into a race against the entry window.A Halloween movie night in Mission HillsValleyween Cinema has published 2026 experiences featuring Hotel Transylvania and Hocus Pocus at Andres Pico Adobe Park in Mission Hills. A seasonal movie event gives a group a shared activity to gather around, especially when everyone wants Halloween atmosphere without choosing a haunted maze.Review the information for the particular performance rather than assuming that every night has the same arrangements. The event’s current listing should explain the date, arrival time, seating, included activities, and what guests need to bring. Those details determine whether the outing suits the people coming with you.A movie night can also be a useful option for a mixed group. Some visitors may want the costumes and decorations more than a scare, while others may be happy simply spending an evening together outside.Community events close to homeSchool and neighborhood calendars can offer another kind of celebration. Valley Charter Elementary’s published school calendar lists a Trunk or Treat on October 24, 2026. Events organized around a school or community can provide a more contained setting than traveling between several attractions.Check who may attend and whether registration is needed before treating a school event as open admission. A calendar entry gives a starting point, while the organizer’s current details establish access, timing, and participation arrangements.Community events can be particularly appealing when the goal is a manageable evening near home. They give you a chance to enjoy the season without making a large attraction the center of the plan.Choose the intensity that fits your groupA pumpkin display, a costumed community gathering, and a haunted attraction are different experiences. Darkness, loud sound, enclosed spaces, uneven surfaces, and performers can affect how comfortable a visitor feels. Age recommendations are worth reviewing alongside the description of the event itself.There is no need to make the biggest event the default choice. One well chosen outing can be more enjoyable than filling every weekend, especially when your household already has school activities, work, and other autumn plans.For a separate look at Halloween night itself, read the trick or treating post. That article focuses on neighborhood routes, participating homes, and practical walking plans, keeping this page focused on seasonal outings.SourcesNight of the Jack, official scheduleMy Valley Pass, Valleyween CinemaValley Charter Elementary, community calendar

blog/homeschool-or-public-school.html.main_text: Homeschool or Public School?September 30, 2026There is no single right answer for every familyChoosing between homeschool and public school can feel like a huge decision because it affects more than academics. It changes the daily schedule, the way children socialize, how parents use their time, and how much control a family has over the learning environment.The better question is not which option is best in general. It is which option fits your child, your household, and the kind of school experience you want right now.What public school can offerPublic school gives children a built in daily routine, access to teachers and support staff, regular interaction with classmates, and a wide range of activities that may include sports, music, clubs, counseling, and special education services.For many families, the biggest advantage is structure. The school day already has a schedule, curriculum, grading system, and staff responsible for instruction. Parents can stay involved without having to design the entire learning day themselves.What homeschool can offerHomeschool can give families more control over pace, curriculum, schedule, and learning style. A child who needs more time in one subject can slow down, while a child who moves quickly can keep going without waiting for the rest of a class.It can also make it easier to build school around travel, family schedules, outside classes, sports, creative interests, or a child who learns better in a quieter setting.The time commitment mattersHomeschooling is not only a school choice, it is also a household commitment. Someone has to plan lessons, supervise work, track progress, find activities, and make sure the child is meeting any state requirements that apply.Public school shifts most of the teaching day to the school, but families still spend time on transportation, homework, school events, communication with teachers, and activities outside the classroom.Social life looks different, not necessarily smallerPublic school makes daily peer interaction automatic because children spend much of the day around classmates. Homeschool families usually have to be more intentional about creating those opportunities through sports, community groups, co ops, classes, faith communities, neighborhood friendships, or other activities.For some children, a large school environment is energizing. For others, smaller and more controlled social settings may be a better fit.Cost can be different tooPublic school does not charge tuition, although families may still pay for supplies, activities, transportation, meals, or after school care.Homeschool costs vary widely. Some families use free or low cost materials, while others pay for full curriculum programs, tutors, online classes, field trips, memberships, and activities. The larger cost can also be the time a parent spends teaching instead of working outside the home.Your child may tell you more than a checklist canA child who is thriving academically, socially, and emotionally in public school may not need a major change. A child who is overwhelmed, bored, anxious, struggling with the environment, or asking for a different way to learn may be giving you useful information.It is also possible for the right answer to change. A family can choose public school for one season and homeschool for another. The decision does not have to define the rest of a child’s education.What should you compare before deciding?Look at your child’s learning style, the quality of the local public school options, your work schedule, your budget, transportation, special learning needs, activities, social opportunities, and how much time an adult can realistically devote to teaching at home.The goal is not to choose the option that sounds best to other people. It is to choose the setting where your child has the strongest chance to learn, grow, and feel supported.ReferencesNational Center for Education Statistics, HomeschoolingNational Center for Education Statistics, Academic Instruction at HomeExplore MoreBlogSearch HomesContact

blog/is-my-property-a-good-fit-for-airbn.main_text: Evaluating Your Property’s Fit for AirbnbOctober 1, 2026Updated October 14, 2026A property’s fit for Airbnb depends on the space being offered and the owner’s ability to support the stay. Once the proposed rental has been confirmed as permitted, the practical decision is whether the home can comfortably accommodate guests and whether the arrangement suits the owner’s life.An appealing location and attractive photographs can bring attention to a property, but they do not describe all the responsibilities that come with it. The guest’s experience begins with arrival and continues through ordinary tasks such as parking, sleeping, cooking, and asking for help when something is unclear.Consider the stay from arrival onwardThink about the physical relationship between the guest space and the rest of the property. An entrance shared with the owner, a separate unit, and a bedroom within the household create different expectations about privacy and access.The property should support the use being described. Stairs, a long route from parking, shared laundry, limited storage, or a bathroom outside the guest area can influence whether the space suits a particular stay. An accurate description helps prospective guests understand those features before committing.Clear boundaries can matter as much as amenities. Owners need to distinguish the spaces available to guests from areas that remain private, especially where personal possessions or everyday household activities share the property.The layout affects comfortSleeping arrangements should be considered alongside bathrooms, circulation, and the living areas guests may use. A stated capacity does not explain whether the property feels comfortable when everyone is present. The layout, privacy, and intended use all matter.Outdoor space brings its own considerations. A patio or garden may be a useful feature, while shared boundaries, nearby bedrooms, or a communal access route may require clearer expectations. The aim is a stay that works within the home’s setting rather than one that creates avoidable friction with the household or neighbors.Ownership still requires attention during a stayGuests may encounter an appliance issue, a plumbing problem, or difficulty accessing the property. The owner needs an appropriate arrangement for handling those situations, including periods when they are unavailable or away from the area.Cleaning, condition checks, maintenance, and communication remain real responsibilities even when a platform manages the reservation itself. A reservation system is one part of the arrangement, while the property still needs someone responsible for its physical condition and the guest’s practical needs.The extent of support required varies with the home. A property with several shared facilities or significant outdoor features can involve a different workload from a simpler space. The useful assessment is based on what this particular property requires.Balance personal use with the proposed rentalAn owner who wants to use the home between stays needs to consider how the rental affects access to personal belongings and the readiness of the space. A household renting a spare room has a different relationship with guests from an owner who will not be present.Neither arrangement should be treated as effortless by default. The question is whether the proposed use fits the owner’s comfort with shared space, schedule, and responsibility. A realistic expectation is more useful than a promise that a particular property type creates easy income.Protect the home while respecting the guestInsurance should be reviewed for the intended activity, and personal items may need appropriate secure storage. Access arrangements should allow the owner to manage the property responsibly while respecting privacy and applicable rules.Any monitoring or security equipment must be evaluated against the relevant law and platform requirements. Ownership of the property does not establish that every device or form of monitoring is appropriate. Clear, lawful expectations support the arrangement more effectively than relying on a guest profile as a guarantee of behavior.Decide whether the arrangement fitsThe practical assessment should leave the owner with a clearer picture of the property’s suitability and the support it needs. It can also establish that another rental arrangement, a different scope, or no rental use is more appropriate.For the detailed regulatory discussion, read the separate Los Angeles rental rules post. Keeping that information there allows this article to focus on the home and the owner’s responsibilities. Dominique can help discuss property management options in relation to the individual property without promising bookings or a particular income.SourcesLos Angeles City Planning, home sharingCalifornia Department of Real Estate, consumer information

blog/places-to-eat-san-fernando-valley.h.main_text: Places to Eat in the San Fernando ValleySeptember 25, 2026A Valley food scene with a little bit of everythingOne of the best things about living in the San Fernando Valley is that a good meal rarely requires leaving the Valley. You can plan a special dinner with a view, sit down for a tasting menu, grab a relaxed neighborhood meal, or meet friends somewhere lively without making the night about a long drive across Los Angeles. The Valley is spread out, so the easiest way to explore it is to think about the kind of experience you want first, then choose the neighborhood.For dinner with a viewOdyssey Restaurant and Events in Granada Hills is one of the Valley's long standing destination restaurants, especially when the view is part of the plan. The hilltop setting looks out over the San Fernando Valley, and the restaurant serves brunch and dinner. It works well for birthdays, date nights, family dinners, and those evenings when you want the setting to feel like part of the occasion.For an intimate tasting experienceEncino has several restaurants that turn dinner into more of an experience. Pasta|Bar offers a small chef counter setting with a multi course tasting menu, while Shin Sushi is known for an intimate omakase format led by the chef. These are the kinds of places to consider when you want the meal itself to be the main event and you are comfortable planning ahead for a reservation.For a lively night outJOEY Woodland Hills is a strong option when you want a polished room, cocktails, and a menu with enough variety for a group. Its Woodland Hills location makes it easy to pair dinner with shopping or an evening around the Warner Center area. The atmosphere is more energetic than quiet, which can make it a good fit for celebrations, group dinners, or a casual date night.For neighborhood flavorThe Valley also has plenty of smaller, casual places that reflect the communities around them. Asumare Peruvian in San Fernando focuses on Peruvian comfort food in a neighborhood setting. El Gallo Giro in San Fernando brings a Mexican restaurant, bakery, and tortilleria style experience, with tacos, tortas, aguas frescas, pan dulce, and other familiar favorites. These are the kinds of places that remind you that a local food guide should not only be about formal dining.Make your own Valley food listThe best San Fernando Valley restaurant list is the one that matches how you actually like to spend your time. Pick one place for a sunset dinner, one for a special tasting menu, one for a casual family meal, and one neighborhood spot you can return to without making it an event. That gives you a much better feel for the Valley than trying to chase one single list of the so called best restaurants.Explore MoreBlogBuyingSellingReferencesOdyssey — official restaurant informationEater LA — San Fernando Valley restaurant guideConsult the linked resource directly for current information, availability, and event details.

blog/studio-city-or-valley-village-which.main_text: Studio City or Valley Village, Which One Should I Choose?October 3, 2026Start with the biggest difference, priceIf you are choosing between Studio City and Valley Village, budget may narrow the decision before anything else does. Dominique’s city pages, with market data current as of August 2026, place Studio City’s median home value at approximately $1.8 million to $1.9 million, while Valley Village is approximately $1.1 million to $1.14 million.That does not mean every Studio City home costs more than every Valley Village home. Condos, townhomes, lot size, condition, street, and location within the neighborhood can change the numbers quickly. It does mean buyers may be comparing two very different price points when they start with detached homes.Studio City feels more connected to Ventura BoulevardStudio City has a strong commercial spine along Ventura Boulevard. Restaurants, grocery stores, fitness studios, cafes, and everyday services are concentrated there, so buyers who like being close to dining and activity may naturally spend more time around that corridor.The neighborhood also gives you quick access toward Hollywood, Burbank, Universal City, and other parts of the Valley. The Universal City and Studio City Metro B Line station adds another transportation option for people who do not want every trip to depend on a car.Valley Village has a quieter residential feelValley Village is close to Studio City and North Hollywood, but much of the neighborhood feels more residential. You can still reach restaurants, grocery stores, cafes, and entertainment nearby, while living on streets that may feel more removed from the busiest commercial areas.That balance can appeal to buyers who want access to the same general part of the Valley without needing to live directly beside its most active corridors.The homes can feel different tooStudio City includes hillside homes, larger single family properties, condos, townhomes, and homes near Ventura Boulevard. Some hillside locations bring views and privacy, but they can also bring additional questions about slope, wildfire exposure, drainage, and insurance.Valley Village is flatter overall and includes a mix of detached homes, condos, townhomes, and smaller multifamily buildings. Buyers who prefer a flatter neighborhood and simpler day to day access may find that important.Think about how you actually spend your weekIf your ideal weekend means walking to a restaurant, being near Ventura Boulevard, heading toward Hollywood, or spending time around Studio City’s busier commercial areas, Studio City may fit the way you already live.If you want a quieter home base, still want quick access to Studio City and North Hollywood, and would rather put more of your budget toward the home itself, Valley Village may deserve a closer look.Schools, transportation, and monthly costs still matterBoth neighborhoods are served by LAUSD, but school assignment is property specific, so buyers should verify the assigned schools for the exact address they are considering.Condo and townhome buyers should also compare HOA dues, parking, insurance, reserves, and the full monthly payment instead of comparing purchase price alone. A lower purchase price does not always mean a lower monthly cost.So, which one should you choose?Choose based on the life you want to have after you get the keys. Studio City may make more sense if you want more activity nearby, direct access to Ventura Boulevard, and are comfortable with the higher price point. Valley Village may make more sense if you want a quieter residential setting, a lower overall entry point, and easy access to nearby Studio City and North Hollywood.The best comparison is not neighborhood versus neighborhood in the abstract. It is the actual Studio City home you could buy with your budget versus the actual Valley Village home you could buy with that same budget.ReferencesStudio City neighborhood guideValley Village neighborhood guideExplore MoreBlogSearch HomesContact

blog/the-different-leagues-of-college-fo.main_text: The Different Leagues of College FootballSeptember 26, 2026First, what is FBS?The Football Bowl Subdivision, usually called FBS, is the highest level of NCAA Division I college football. Within FBS, schools are grouped into conferences.The conferences have their own schedules, championship races, rivalries and histories. Once you understand the conferences, the sport becomes much easier to follow.Big TenFor Southern California fans, this is probably the conference that changed the most locally because USC and UCLA are both Big Ten programs now.That puts the two Los Angeles schools in the same conference as programs such as Ohio State, Michigan, Penn State, Oregon, Washington, Iowa and Wisconsin. The Big Ten is known for huge stadiums, long established rivalries and several of the most recognizable brands in college football.SECThe SEC is the Southeastern Conference. It includes programs such as Alabama, Georgia, LSU, Texas, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Florida.The conference is closely associated with national championship expectations, NFL talent and enormous football culture throughout the South. Texas and Oklahoma joining the SEC made an already deep league even bigger.ACCThe Atlantic Coast Conference includes traditional programs such as Clemson, Florida State and Miami, while Stanford and Cal are also part of the conference now.That means a league once identified almost entirely with the East Coast now reaches all the way to California. The ACC champion receives an automatic place in the College Football Playoff under the current format.Big 12The Big 12 also changed dramatically through realignment. Programs such as Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado, BYU and Utah became part of the modern Big 12 after the old Pac 12 structure changed.The conference also includes schools such as Texas Tech, Oklahoma State, Kansas State, Baylor and TCU. The Big 12 can feel especially wide open because several programs may realistically compete for the conference championship in the same season.Pac 12The Pac 12 returned in a new form for 2026. Oregon State and Washington State were joined by Boise State, Colorado State, Fresno State, San Diego State, Texas State and Utah State as football members.It is not the old Pac 12 that included USC, UCLA, Oregon, Washington, Stanford and Cal, but it gives western college football another regional conference identity.What about the other FBS conferences?The American, Conference USA, Mid American Conference, Mountain West and Sun Belt also play FBS football.These conferences may receive less national attention than the Big Ten, SEC, ACC and Big 12, but they still matter in the playoff structure. The highest ranked team from the American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac 12 or Sun Belt receives an automatic playoff bid.So where do USC and UCLA fit now?Both are Big Ten programs. That is still strange for people who grew up watching the old Pac 10 or Pac 12.A USC or UCLA conference schedule can now include schools from the Midwest and East Coast. The geography may look unusual, but modern college football realignment has made the sport much more national.How does the College Football Playoff work?The 2026 season uses a 12 team playoff. The champions of the ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC receive automatic bids. The highest ranked team from the American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac 12 or Sun Belt also receives an automatic bid.The remaining spots are awarded through the final College Football Playoff rankings. First round games are played on campus, then the quarterfinals and semifinals move into the bowl system.Why do the conferences matter so much?Conference membership affects a team's schedule, championship race, recruiting, television exposure, travel, rivalries and route into the playoff.College football is not one league with identical divisions. It is a collection of conferences that eventually collide in the postseason. Once you understand that, Saturdays become much easier to follow.ReferencesNCAA, How the College Football Playoff WorksCollege Football Playoff, 2026 Playoff FormatPac 12 Conference, 2026 Football ScheduleExplore MoreBlogSearch HomesContact

blog/trick-or-treating-san-fernando-vall.main_text: Trick or Treating in the San Fernando ValleySeptember 23, 2026Updated October 14, 2026Trick or treating in the San Fernando Valley works best when the route, pace, and expectations fit the people walking together. A familiar neighborhood can provide a satisfying Halloween evening without needing a famous destination or a long drive.The practical choices come early, including where to begin, how far to walk, who stays together, and how everyone will get home. Sorting those out leaves more attention for costumes, decorated porches, and the pleasure of seeing neighbors outside.Choose a route you can comfortably manageStart with the streets your group can navigate without repeated complicated crossings. Look for usable sidewalks, a clear walking route, and places where you can cross at intersections. A short route with a straightforward return can be easier to enjoy than a long loop chosen only for the number of decorated houses.If you are visiting an unfamiliar area, understand the parking and walking arrangements before the evening begins. Avoid relying on a plan that requires frequent stops by car while children move between houses. Driveways, parked vehicles, and busy crossings deserve attention even on streets that appear residential and relaxed.The route should also reflect the group’s pace. Younger children, a stroller, someone using a mobility aid, or a visitor who tires easily can change what makes a comfortable outing. A natural place to turn back helps keep the evening flexible.Make the group plan clearAgree on who is supervising younger children and whether older children will remain with the group. If anyone is permitted to walk separately, establish a meeting place and a way to check in. Make those decisions before the excitement of the evening makes communication harder.Consider the practical parts of a costume as well as its appearance. The wearer needs to see clearly and walk without tripping. Visibility matters around traffic, and reflective details or lights can help a driver notice someone moving near the road.A flashlight can also help people see the path, changes in level, and obstacles. Keep attention on the surroundings when walking and crossing, especially where vehicles may be entering or leaving driveways.Let participating homes set the invitationHalloween decorations can be part of the neighborhood atmosphere without meaning that every property welcomes visitors. Approach homes that appear to be participating, follow any signs or directions, and respect a closed gate or an unlit entrance.Stay on the intended path to the door and give other groups room to pass. Gardens, planters, parked vehicles, and decorative displays are part of someone’s home. Treating them carefully helps the evening remain enjoyable for residents as well as visitors.If a particular display is too intense for someone in your group, moving past it is a reasonable choice. The evening should leave room for different comfort levels without making every stop compulsory.Give drivers and pedestrians roomHalloween can bring more people into the street at the same time that residents are returning home or driving to other plans. Cross where drivers can reasonably expect pedestrians, and avoid stepping into the road from between parked cars.Drivers should slow down, remain attentive, and look carefully around crossings and driveways. Children may move unpredictably, especially when their attention is on friends, costumes, or the next participating house. A less hurried pace helps both groups share the neighborhood.Keep the finish as simple as the startHave a realistic point at which the group will head home. Comfortable footwear, water, and a bag that is easy to carry can make the walk more pleasant, but flexibility matters too. Ending earlier is fine when the people taking part have had enough.For organized attractions, movie nights, and seasonal community events, use the separate Halloween activities post. This page is about the neighborhood evening itself, the route, the company, and a respectful way to enjoy the homes around you.SourcesNational Highway Traffic Safety Administration, Halloween safetyLos Angeles Fire Department, public safety information

blog/van-nuys-or-reseda-which-one-should.main_text: Van Nuys or Reseda, Which One Should I Choose?October 2, 2026The prices are closer than you might expectDominique’s city pages, with market data current as of August 2026, place Van Nuys at approximately $817,000 to $830,000 for the median home value, while Reseda is approximately $805,000 to $810,000.Because those ranges are relatively close, this comparison is less about assuming one neighborhood is the cheaper choice and more about looking at the specific house, lot, condition, street, and monthly ownership costs.Van Nuys gives you a very central Valley locationVan Nuys sits near major north and south routes and gives buyers access to the 405, the 101, and the 170 through nearby corridors. It also has Metrolink service and access to the Metro G Line.For someone whose week involves driving in several different directions across the Valley, that central location may be one of the strongest reasons to consider Van Nuys.Reseda has a strong West Valley connectionReseda sits farther west and gives buyers convenient access toward Northridge, Tarzana, Encino, Woodland Hills, and other West Valley areas. The Metro G Line runs through Reseda and connects toward North Hollywood.If your work, family, shopping, or daily routine is already centered farther west, Reseda may make more sense even when two homes look similar on paper.Compare the actual homes, not just the ZIP codeBoth neighborhoods have many detached homes without an HOA, along with condos, townhomes, and smaller multifamily properties. Lot size, parking, renovations, accessory dwelling units, street traffic, and condition can vary significantly from one block to another.That makes it especially important to compare what your budget buys in each neighborhood at the same moment, rather than deciding from a neighborhood reputation alone.Everyday convenience looks a little differentVan Nuys Boulevard, Sepulveda Boulevard, and the Civic Center area give Van Nuys a large concentration of stores, restaurants, services, medical access, and government offices. The Van Nuys and Sherman Oaks Recreation Center and the Sepulveda Basin also add substantial recreation nearby.Reseda Boulevard and Sherman Way are major everyday corridors in Reseda, with shopping, restaurants, services, and easy access toward Northridge and Tarzana. Reseda Park is a major neighborhood recreation space.Think about the commute before the house wins you overA home can look perfect during a showing and feel very different after a week of commuting. Before choosing between Van Nuys and Reseda, test the drive or transit trip you will actually make at the time of day you will actually make it.Ten or fifteen minutes on a map can feel much larger when it is repeated every morning and evening.So, which one should you choose?Van Nuys may fit you better if a central Valley location, Metrolink access, and easier movement toward several parts of Los Angeles matter most. Reseda may fit you better if your life is centered farther west and you like the access toward Northridge, Tarzana, and the West Valley.Because the median values are so close, I would let the specific property decide the final round. Compare the homes you can actually buy, then compare the commute, street, condition, monthly costs, and how each location fits your routine.ReferencesVan Nuys neighborhood guideReseda neighborhood guideExplore MoreBlogSearch HomesContact

blog-401k-matters.html.main_text: 401K MattersOctober 6, 2026A 401(k) is a workplace retirement plan that can help you prepare for life beyond your working years. It deserves a place in your financial plan alongside housing, current bills, and emergency savings. Start by understanding what your employer’s plan offers and how its contributions fit your budget.Know what happens on paydayEligible employees can generally direct part of their pay into a 401(k). Traditional pretax contributions generally reduce current federal taxable income, while designated Roth contributions, if the plan offers them, are made after tax. Qualified Roth distributions can be tax-free. Eligibility, contribution limits, and withdrawal rules matter; review the plan and current IRS guidance before choosing an approach.Understand the employer contributionIf your employer offers a match, ask how it is calculated and what you must contribute to receive it. Also ask about vesting: some employer contributions become yours over time under the plan’s rules. A contribution example on a statement does not mean every employer offers the same arrangement.Read more than the account balanceReview contribution elections, the investments selected, fees, beneficiaries, and the plan’s Summary Plan Description. An account can gain or lose value, and fees affect what remains. If the terminology feels unfamiliar, ask the plan administrator to explain it before making a change.Keep retirement and home goals in the same conversationA down payment can feel urgent because it has an immediate destination. Retirement may feel farther away, but both goals compete for the same monthly income. Put a proposed housing payment beside retirement contributions, everyday expenses, and an emergency reserve. That comparison helps you see whether a home fits your broader priorities.Do not treat a withdrawal as ordinary savingsA retirement account is subject to access and tax rules. A distribution before age 59½ can bring an additional 10% tax unless an exception applies, and other taxes may also apply. A plan loan, if available, has its own terms. Before using retirement money for a purchase or emergency, discuss the consequences with the plan administrator and a qualified tax or financial professional.Turn a statement into a useful conversationYou do not have to settle every retirement decision in one afternoon. Confirm your current contribution, understand the match and fees, and choose a time to review the plan again. When a housing decision comes up, bring that information into your budget so the move supports both your present life and the future you are building.Related readingThe Power of a BudgetReferencesIRS — Topic No. 424: 401(k) PlansIRS — Designated Roth AccountsU.S. Department of Labor — What You Should Know About Your Retirement Plan

blog-california-condo-crisis-sb326-2026..main_text: California’s Condo Crisis: What SB 326 Means for Buyers and Sellers in 2026October 8, 2026California’s SB 326 balcony inspection requirements can reveal repairs that an HOA’s reserves cannot cover. Those costs may become special assessments for owners. Combined with condo lending changes and insurance requirements, the association’s condition and financial health deserve as much attention as the unit itself.What SB 326 actually requiresSB 326 applies to qualifying exterior elevated elements in condominium buildings with three or more units: balconies, decks, stairs, and walkways more than six feet above ground that rely substantially on wood or wood-based load-bearing supports. The inspection addresses supporting components and associated waterproofing, rather than simply how a balcony looks.The initial inspection deadline for covered condominium associations was January 1, 2025. Subsequent inspections are required at least every nine years. This is different from the separate apartment-building inspection law, SB 721.A licensed architect or structural engineer evaluates a statistically significant sample. The inspection method depends on the conditions; opening walls is not automatically required in every inspection. Reports document findings and recommended repairs. Safety concerns can require restricted access and prompt action.The special assessment shockWhen reserves fall short, owners may face a special assessment to pay for repairs. LS Carlson Law reports assessments of $40,000–$60,000 per unit in some affected communities. That is a reported range, not a statewide average or a prediction for every building.The monthly dues on a listing never tell the whole story. As a hypothetical comparison, a $450 monthly HOA payment with a possible $50,000 assessment could present a very different financial commitment from $700 monthly dues in an association with funded repairs and healthy reserves. Compare the documents and planned work, not just the advertised payment.Fannie Mae changed the lending review in August 2026Fannie Mae retired its Limited Review process for loan applications dated on or after August 3, 2026. Lenders must use the applicable remaining project-review pathway or a permitted waiver. Depending on the project and loan, that can mean closer review of the association’s finances, repairs, insurance, litigation, and other eligibility requirements.A project that is ineligible for Fannie Mae financing can limit a buyer’s lending options. It does not mean every possible conventional or portfolio loan is unavailable. Ask the lender to confirm the specific building’s eligibility early.For applications dated on or after January 4, 2027, the standard minimum reserve allocation under Full Review increases from 10% to 15% of annual budgeted assessment income. A qualifying reserve-study alternative may apply. This budget allocation is different from a reserve study’s “percent funded,” which compares reserve assets with estimated reserve obligations. Do not treat those two percentages as interchangeable.Insurance can complicate a transactionCondo financing also depends on acceptable project insurance. Coverage amounts, deductibles, exclusions, and policy terms can affect eligibility even when the buyer is financially qualified. Have the lender review the master policy early, alongside the inspection and financial documents.What buyers should doRequest the latest inspection report. Ask for the exterior elevated elements report and any repair or follow-up documentation. California’s Department of Real Estate identifies the report among common-interest development disclosures.Ask about assessments. Find out what is approved, proposed, or being discussed, what work it covers, and how payment responsibility will be handled in your contract.Read the reserve study and budget together. Look at planned projects, funding recommendations, and the association’s actual allocation.Review other project risks. Discuss delinquency, litigation, meeting minutes, and repair findings with the appropriate professionals.Confirm financing and insurance early. Your lender should assess the building, not only your personal loan application.What sellers should doCollect the HOA’s inspection report, repair information, budget, reserve study, insurance details, and assessment notices before listing. Unresolved questions can become renegotiations or delays once a buyer’s lender begins reviewing the project.Explain documented facts clearly and work with your agent, HOA, lender, and qualified advisers to resolve gaps. A well-prepared disclosure package helps buyers understand the property’s full financial picture.This is general real estate information, not legal or financial advice. Requirements and loan eligibility depend on the project and transaction; verify them with the HOA, lender, and a qualified professional.Related readingBuying a home with DominiqueHOA documents to gather before listingReferencesCalifornia Civil Code §5551 — condominium exterior elevated element inspectionsCalifornia Department of Real Estate — common-interest development disclosuresFannie Mae — Lender Letter LL-2026-03, project standards and insurance updatesFannie Mae — Full Review processLS Carlson Law — reported special assessment ranges

blog-california-proposition-19-homeowner.main_text: What Is California Proposition 19, and How Does It Affect San Fernando Valley Homeowners?October 12, 2026California Proposition 19 changes how eligible homeowners transfer a home’s taxable value when they move, and how some inherited family homes qualify for reassessment relief. These are different provisions with different requirements, so a benefit available when selling and buying a home does not automatically apply to an inheritance.Why it matters when life changesA home can hold decades of memories, yet stop fitting everyday life. You may want fewer stairs, a different layout, less upkeep or a location closer to the people you rely on.For families handling an inherited home, the decisions can be more complicated. The practical questions about keeping, selling or living in the property often arrive alongside an emotional transition.Proposition 19 may be part of those conversations, but the first step is understanding which situation applies to you.Moving to another primary residenceEligible homeowners age 55 or older, people with a qualifying severe and permanent disability, and qualifying wildfire or natural disaster victims may transfer their existing taxable value to a replacement primary residence anywhere in California.The sale and replacement purchase or new construction must satisfy the required two year timing window. A higher value replacement can result in an adjustment, so preserving a taxable value does not promise an unchanged total tax bill.The benefit requires a claim to the appropriate county assessor. It is not automatically completed through escrow. Confirm eligibility and timing before relying on it in your moving plans.An inherited home follows different rulesQualifying transfers of family homes between parents and children, and certain grandparents and grandchildren, may receive limited reassessment relief. Principal residence use, value limits, exemption filings and exclusion claims matter.The family home must meet the required residence rules, including becoming the eligible recipient’s principal residence within one year. The homeowners’ or disabled veterans’ exemption should be claimed within one year to receive relief from the transfer date. Certain late claims may receive prospective relief, so ask the assessor before assuming every option is lost. A rental or second home is not automatically protected by this family home exclusion.Keep the property decision and the tax decision connectedA move should still fit your daily needs. A potential tax benefit does not tell you whether a particular home, location or timeline is right for you.Likewise, keeping an inherited home is a personal and practical decision. Consider how you would use it and what owning it would involve, while getting advice specific to the estate and property.Dominique can help you explore the real estate side of your plans. Your county assessor, tax adviser and attorney can address eligibility, filings and the legal consequences of a transfer.Get guidance before committing to a planDominique is a Realtor, not an attorney or tax adviser. This article provides general information, not legal or tax advice. Confirm the current rules and your particular circumstances with the county assessor and qualified advisers.If a move or an inherited home is part of your next chapter, start a conversation with Dominique about the property and the options you want to explore.Sources and current informationCalifornia State Board of Equalization, Proposition 19 guidance and filing requirementsCalifornia State Board of Equalization, Proposition 19 Fact SheetDetails checked October 12, 2026. blog-chatsworth-home-prices-2026.html.main_text: What Does It Cost to Buy a Home in Chatsworth, California Right Now?October 11, 2026Redfin’s Chatsworth market page, checked October 11, 2026, shows a median sale price of $929,500 and median time on market of 49 days for its displayed August 2026 reporting period. These are closed-sale indicators, not a quote for a particular home or a live October listing price.That headline number tells you the middle of the market — but Chatsworth actually has three very different price lanes, and knowing which one fits your budget changes your whole search strategy.The three price lanes in ChatsworthCondos: the $500s. As an illustrative search budget, a condo in the $500,000 range with monthly HOA dues may be an entry point. Check current listings and association documents for actual prices and fees. Condos are the most affordable way into Chatsworth — but California buyers should know what they're signing up for. New balcony inspection rules under SB 326 mean HOAs in older buildings may be budgeting for big repairs, and those costs land on owners through dues or special assessments. Always read the HOA budget and reserve study before you fall in love with a condo.Townhomes: the $600s. A townhome in the $600,000 range is another illustrative search budget; availability and HOA costs vary by community. Townhomes give you more space than a condo with less maintenance than a house — a solid middle ground for first-time buyers who want a garage and a yard patch without the full weight of a single-family home.Single-family homes: the $700s and up. Some buyers start searching in the $700,000 range, but size, condition, lot, and location can move a detached home well above that. The $929,500 figure above covers all home types, not only detached houses. Compare recent sales of similar detached homes rather than applying the overall neighborhood median to every house.What sellers should knowRedfin’s displayed sale-to-list ratio is 98.9%. That is a market-wide measure, not a promise that every home will sell near asking price or within seven weeks. If you're thinking about selling in the San Fernando Valley, a pricing conversation grounded in this week's data — not last spring's headlines — is where I always start.What buyers should knowCondos and townhomes in the $500s–$600s are Chatsworth's entry point, and they come with a real question to run past your lender: can you comfortably carry the payment plus HOA dues plus taxes and insurance? Run all four numbers before you write an offer, not after.Reading the numbers correctlyThe three price lanes are starting points for a search, not verified active listings or guaranteed price bands. Listing prices and closed-sale medians measure different things. Ask for current comparable sales and available homes before setting an offer price.ReferencesRedfin — Chatsworth housing market, reporting period shown on the pageResources checked October 11, 2026. blog-dia-de-los-muertos-san-fernando-val.main_text: Celebrating Día de los Muertos in the San Fernando ValleyOctober 12, 2026Día de los Muertos is a time to remember loved ones through flowers, photographs, food and shared stories. In the San Fernando Valley, San Fernando Mission Cemetery has announced its 2026 observance for Saturday, November 7, with Mass at noon and a cultural celebration beginning at 1:30 p.m.A celebration of memory and loveDía de los Muertos, traditionally observed around November 1 and 2, brings remembrance into everyday life. Its Mexican traditions combine Indigenous heritage and Catholic observances, with practices that vary between families and communities.An ofrenda is a personal tribute. Photographs recall familiar faces, marigolds bring color, and favorite foods or treasured objects connect the altar to the person being remembered. Pan de muerto and papel picado are familiar parts of many celebrations, but every family’s observance has its own meaning.For children, an altar can become a way to hear stories about relatives they knew and those they never had the chance to meet. For adults, it offers a place to pause, remember and share something that might otherwise go unsaid.A confirmed 2026 celebration in Mission HillsSan Fernando Mission Cemetery, at 11160 Stranwood Avenue in Mission Hills, will hold its Día de los Muertos observance on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The organizer’s published schedule lists Mass and the blessing of the altars at noon, followed by music, children’s activities and folkloric dancers at 1:30 p.m. The event ends at 6 p.m.The cemetery setting makes remembrance central to the occasion. Visitors can take time to appreciate the altars while respecting the families who created them and the people resting there.Check Catholic Cemeteries & Mortuaries for the latest event information before attending. If you hope to display an altar, check registration directly with the organizer rather than assuming space is available. The published page currently marks San Fernando altar registration as closed.Finding celebrations close to homeThe City of San Fernando and other Valley communities share seasonal cultural programming through their own calendars and announcements. Look for current organizer information before choosing a date, since a previous year’s schedule may still appear in an event roundup.A public celebration can be a thoughtful introduction to the tradition. Go with curiosity, listen to the stories being shared, and ask before photographing a family’s altar or participating in a private observance.The meaning of homeA home holds more than furniture and belongings. It holds the meals people shared, the conversations that ran late, and the small routines that become family memories.An ofrenda brings those memories into view. A photograph on a shelf or a familiar recipe on the table can remind us how much of home is shaped by the people we love.That connection between place and belonging is part of what makes the Valley worth getting to know. If you are considering a move here, Dominique can help you explore the communities and homes that fit your next chapter.Sources and current informationCatholic Cemeteries & Mortuaries, 2026 celebrations and scheduleCatholic Cemeteries & Mortuaries, remembrance and altar traditionsCity of San Fernando, community announcementsDetails checked October 12, 2026. Schedules and availability can change. The photograph is an illustration.

blog-fall-farmers-markets-san-fernando-v.main_text: Fall Farmers Markets in the San Fernando Valley, Where to Shop This SeasonOctober 12, 2026Fall is a lovely time to explore the San Fernando Valley’s farmers markets. Evening options in Northridge and Granada Hills, Tuesday markets in Sherman Oaks and at CSUN, and the Sunday Studio City market offer different ways to enjoy seasonal produce and neighborhood life. Forneris Farms in Mission Hills also has pumpkins in 2026, but no corn maze this year.The pleasures of shopping in seasonAn autumn market gives you room to enjoy more than a grocery list. Pumpkins and winter squash bring color to the stalls, while persimmons, pomegranates and other seasonal produce help make an ordinary shopping trip feel connected to the time of year.What is available changes with harvests and individual vendors. Some stalls sell locally grown produce, others offer prepared food, bread or specialty goods. Ask the seller about the items that catch your eye rather than assuming every product is organic or grown nearby.Markets also offer a simple way to spend time in a neighborhood. A familiar stall, a quick conversation and something good to take home can become part of a weekly routine.Wednesday evenings in NorthridgeThe Northridge Farmers Market and Family Festival operates Wednesdays from 5 to 9 p.m. at 9301 Tampa Avenue. Coastal Pacific Markets lists the 2026 season as March 11 through October 28, making October the final part of this year’s scheduled season.It is an evening option for people who want to visit after work or school. Check the organizer’s announcements before heading out, particularly near the end of the season or if weather may affect the event.Friday nights in Granada HillsThe Granada Hills Chamber of Commerce lists its Certified Farmers Market on Fridays from 6 to 10 p.m., around White Oak Avenue and Chatsworth Street. The chamber also promotes the Granada Grubfest alongside the market.Fresh produce, artisanal goods and food vendors can make this an outing rather than a quick errand. For the current layout and vendor information, use the chamber’s market page.Tuesday shopping in Sherman Oaks and at CSUNThe Sherman Oaks Farmers Market is a weekday option, not a weekend market. Its operator, Raw Inspiration, lists Tuesdays from 2 to 6 p.m. at 14006 Riverside Drive, by Fashion Square.At CSUN, Associated Students lists the campus farmers market in Matador Square on Tuesdays during the fall and spring semesters, from 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Because it follows the academic calendar, check the university’s current event information before making a special trip.Sunday mornings in Studio CityThe Studio City Farmers Market’s own website now lists Sunday hours from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Ventura Place, between Radford Avenue and Laurel Canyon Boulevard. The market operates rain or shine and offers produce, artisanal foods and a children’s section.A morning visit leaves time to explore the surrounding neighborhood afterward. Check the market’s website for parking information and any announcements before you go.A farm stand stop in Mission HillsForneris Farms, at 15200 Rinaldi Street in Mission Hills, offers a different experience from a weekly street market. The family farm lists its market hours as 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily, with earlier closing on holidays.For 2026, the farm says it will have pumpkins but no corn maze. It also states that the farm market is cash only and that the fields are not open for self harvesting. Check its pumpkin patch information for the current seasonal arrangements.A farm stand visit is a chance to enjoy a piece of the Valley’s agricultural history while shopping for what the season brings.A small ritual that makes a place familiarMarkets are one way to experience a community beyond its housing listings. They let you see ordinary neighborhood life, from the morning coffee stop to the evening crowd gathering around food stalls.A lively market does not guarantee that a neighborhood or home will suit every buyer. It is one part of the picture, alongside the location, your daily routine and the property itself.If a Valley community has caught your attention, Dominique can help you explore homes there and compare your options.Sources and current informationCoastal Pacific Markets, Northridge season and hoursGranada Hills Chamber of Commerce, Friday marketRaw Inspiration, Sherman Oaks marketCSUN Associated Students, campus farmers marketStudio City Farmers Market, current Sunday hoursForneris Farms, 2026 seasonal informationDetails checked October 12, 2026. Schedules and availability can change. The photograph is an illustration.

blog-film-crew-rental.html.main_text: Can You Rent Your San Fernando Valley Home to a Film Crew?October 11, 2026Yes — a home can earn income as a production location, subject to the agreement and local requirements. The production needs your written permission, and in the City of Los Angeles commercial on-location filming generally requires a filming permit on private property as well as public property. FilmLA coordinates permits; an owner’s permission does not replace the city permit.This isn't theoretical for me. Before I became a Realtor, I ran a property management company in Atlanta where we rented out vacant homes as production locations for music videos and commercials. I've seen what a well-managed shoot looks like — and what a badly managed one does to a house.How it actually worksLocation scouts find homes through location libraries, agencies, or simply driving neighborhoods. If your home has the right look — a mid-century kitchen, a pool, a craftsman exterior — a scout may knock on your door or leave a note. Compensation is negotiated per production and depends on the size of the shoot, the number of days, and which parts of the home they use.The paperwork that protects youA written location release. Never agree verbally. The release should spell out exactly which rooms and areas are included, the dates and hours, the crew size, and what happens if they need the kitchen after all — get changes added in writing on the day, not after.Before-and-after photos. Photograph every room on day one. It settles damage arguments fast and is the single cheapest insurance policy you'll ever buy.Cleanup and restoration terms. The contract should say the home is returned to its pre-shoot condition, with a timeline.Your mortgage and insurance. Check your homeowner's insurance and mortgage terms before you sign — some policies need to know about commercial use of the home.Don't forget your neighborsShare dates and hours with neighbors through lawful direct communication. Coordinate required neighborhood notifications with the production and FilmLA; a personal note does not replace the official process. Productions also carry liability insurance for the shoot, and legitimate companies will show you their paperwork without being asked. If a production can't produce a release, insurance, or a permit plan, that's your sign to walk away.Why this matters for Valley homeownersThe San Fernando Valley has homes and residential settings that may interest location scouts for commercials, music videos, and other productions. A distinctive home can become an income stream between tenants, between listings, or alongside your own use. That's exactly the kind of income strategy I help homeowners think through as part of my property management work.Before signingConfirm the exact jurisdiction, permits, insurance, payment terms, crew access, and responsibility for damage with the production. Location use differs from short-term or mid-term lodging. Discuss the proposed agreement with your insurer and an attorney; income and bookings are not guaranteed.ReferencesFilmLA — City of Los Angeles filming requirementsFilmLA — How to get a film permitResources checked October 11, 2026.
